summary: Lita Peipina is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Peking University (~1956–1961) under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian, and served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1961–2014).

Liz Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (1985–1992), where she was also a lecturer (1991–1992), before becoming Associate Professor of Religion at Miami University in 1992.
Liza Zigmund-Cerbu (1924–1965) was a religious studies scholar. She studied at both the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in 1947.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Aganina (1926–2000) worked in Indology and linguistics. She served on the editorial staff of Sovetskoe vostokovedenie (1954–1958) and became a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1958.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Mervart (1888–1965) studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1910) and worked in Indology and linguistics. Her career included posts at Far Eastern Federal University, Kunstkamera, the Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Choedak specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned an Acharya degree at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2012–2013), worked on The Great History of U-Tsang at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (2013–2018), and lectured at CIHTS in 2018.

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (until 1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and with Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its head until 1997, and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies in 1991.

Lozang Jamspal is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Ram Shankar Tripathi. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Delhi, CIHTS, and Columbia University.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri, and taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin (b. 1939), a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries under the 14th Dalai Lama and Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa. He held leadership posts at Central Schools for Tibetans and served as Director of CIHTS (~1988–2000).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (b. 1937), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College, director of CIHTS (1988–2001), president of the Association of Indian Universities, and chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He has held positions at Columbia University, Cambridge, MPIWG, the University of Bonn, and a postdoctoral fellowship at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2026).

Loden Sherab Dagyab (b. 1940) studied at Drepung Monastery under the 14th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House in New Delhi (1964–1966), became a Tibetologist at the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibet House Germany in 2005.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).
